classification: Independent acceptance of the exact compact KloostDens supplier
conclusions: The theorem retains the original OmLong and OmBlock quotient coordinates and psi_beta(z)=exp(i Re(beta*z)). The scaled complex Haar measure is exactly abs(beta)/(2*pi) times Lebesgue measure in each source coordinate.

The change X=t*v, B=t*b, rho=t*a*J_n*u_v has real Jacobian abs(t)^(n*(n+3)); the nonlinear dependence on v is triangular. Replacing rho_0 by sigma contributes abs(t)^(2*n)*abs(A)^(-2). Thus the reduced integral has exactly the displayed abs(t)^(-n*(n+1)) factor.
The determinant sign is D-prime=(-1)^n*D. Row reversal and the actual entry permutation give the stated Hessenberg matrix; the original corner/subdiagonal phase becomes (rho_0+sum x_i)/t exactly.
The cofactor-zero set is null because for fixed nonzero t it is the zero set of a nonzero polynomial in the original coordinates. Fixed t,c quotient properness justifies the initial variable changes.

The crucial support argument is uniform as t tends to zero: bounded matrix entries bound q_t,x,Y, while A*q_t+B0=D-prime and B0=O(abs(t)) force A away from zero. Since A-product(x_i)=O(abs(t)), all x_i stay away from zero. The common compact cutoff and all derivative bounds for a_t are therefore justified, including arbitrary arguments of t.

The quotient (q_t-q_0)/t is holomorphic in t near zero on the common compact support, so a_t-a_0=O(abs(t)) in each fixed smooth seminorm. No singular-t dominated-convergence assumption is substituted.

The critical points are precisely x=(z,...,z), z^(n+1)=D-prime. The complex Hessian is z^(-1)*(I+ones), with determinant (n+1)*z^(-n). The real Hessian pairs positive and negative directions via multiplication by i, hence has signature zero and determinant magnitude abs(beta)^(2*n)*abs(det H)^2.

The compact stationary-phase theorem supplies O(abs(t)^(n+1)) in the reduced integral. Uniformity in arg(t) follows from a compact circle of phases with fixed critical points, uniformly nonsingular Hessians and a uniform lower bound for the gradient off their neighborhoods. The same finite-seminorm bound for norm-one functionals proves the Banach-valued remainder.

The normalized measure cancels (2*pi)^n and abs(beta)^n in the stationary coefficient. Differentiating the determinant gives dq_t/dt at zero = sum adjacent Y entries divided by z; the exact scaling Y=z*v then gives abs(z)^(n*(n+1)). The final coefficient is precisely abs(z)^(n*n)/(n+1), with phase psi_beta((n+1)*z/t) and O(abs(t)) remainder.

Partial averaging of a compact function supported in GL_N has compact smooth support in the remaining invertible block: fixed-head Gaussian recovery bounds its entries, the head inverse and radical variables, and det C=det Z/det H stays away from zero. Extension by zero across singular C is therefore smooth.

Freezing the final singleton c first produces a compact smooth invertible-block function whose regular orbital integrals are original regular orbital integrals. Induction at rank N-1 proves all heads ending in that singleton. The long-block germ then handles every other final block at rank N, without requiring an induction on a false full-lower-group quotient.

All root coefficients have the same nonzero modulus. Annular averaging against the conjugate selected character annihilates every other distinct frequency and the O(1/abs(x)) error. This isolates each required long-block orbital value.
The explicit Lebesgue-to-mu_beta factors for the long and two-block integrals are nonzero and retained. Source cStd=-2*i and betaU=-cStd=2*i, so the original KloostDens phase is covered.

For a relevant invertible weighted permutation head, equality with hMat fixes the permutation and its nonzero diagonal entries. Thus the theorem applies to every sigma,d representation quantified by the original KloostDens interface.
